Body-mounted 3U panels in the SOA tables give about 8 W per face (8–8.4 W) at 54–76 W/kg.
3U deployable arrays in the SOA tables give 7–21.6 W at 33–75 W/kg.
Articulated (sun-tracking) small-satellite wings in the SOA tables reach about 30–31 W/kg; a 3U body-mount plus deployed array gives 28–42 W.

CubeSat UHF transceivers send typically 9.6 kbps (0.1–38.4 kbps) and weigh 22–158 g. At 38.4 kbps, 30 minutes of contact a day returns about 0.26 GB a month.
CubeSat S-band transmitters send 1–20 Mbps and weigh 70–1360 g. The game scales S-band and X-band data volume down, together with the instruments' data volume.

nasaRef.text: CubeSat onboard computers draw about 0.1–5 W. Typical commercial boards tolerate a total ionizing dose of 20–40 krad and rad-hard units 100 krad. Memory runs from hundreds of KB to several GB.

Passive magnetic stabilization has flown on CubeSats (CubeSat 101). The SOA lists coarse 3U buses at <15° pointing.
A 3-axis magnetorquer board weighs about 0.2 kg and draws 0.4–1.2 W; sun sensors are 0.1–5° accurate. Magnetorquers alone cannot hold 3-axis attitude, so pointing stays coarse.
Integrated CubeSat ADCS units (3 reaction wheels, magnetorquers and a star tracker) weigh 0.26–1.813 kg and point to between <1° and 0.003°. Star trackers are 2–40 arcsec accurate.
